The code described in this document was designed based on the
FOG-COA and AID-FOG ManGO flows with the goal to address situations
in which we need to **validate filenames based on a variety of
regular expressions and custom functions and move the corresponding
iRODS data objects based on the result**.

```{python}
import patterns
```

# Description

The `patterns` module defines three classes:

- `Pattern`, representing a combination of a regular expression to
and zero or more functions to validate against.

    + The regex pattern is expected to have named capturing groups.
    + The validation functions have to take a dictionary of
    filename properties (e.g. extracted from the capturing groups)
    and only return something (a string) when validation fails.
    + It also includes a jinja template to build a destination path
    for the filename if it passes the validations.

- `PatternSet`, representing a collection of `Pattern`s to
validate against.

    + It has a `jinja2` environment with optionally custom filters
    that can be shared by all its `Pattern`s.
    + It can have validation functions to be shared by all its
    `Pattern`s.
    + It can have a normalization function to pre-process the
    path before it goes into a validation loop.

- `Filename`, representing a path to validate and eventually move.

    + It has a `path` attribute with the original path.
    + It has a `params` dictionary with at least the "filename" key
    and the name of the file as value. More parameters can be set
    manually or, by successful validation against a `Pattern`,
    from the named groups of the regular expressions or even
    the validation functions.
    + It has a basic `jinja2` environment used to fill in a
    `destination_path` template, meant for when no validation passes.
    + It can be validated against a `Pattern`; if it passes,
    its `params` are updated and it inherits the `Pattern`'s
    `jinja2` environment and `destination_path` template.
    + A `log_result()` method defines a dictionary of information
    to report on the conditions of the `Filename`.
    + The `postprocess_in_irods()` method is the only one that
    actually requires an `iRODSSession`;
    it allows us to do something with iRODS if necessary and returns
    the same log dictionary.

# Examples

## The `Filename` class

When instantiating a `Filename` class, you need at least a path,
but you can optionally provide a dictionary of properties `params`
and a custom `jinja2` template as `invalid_destination_pattern`.

```{python}
# basic filename
fname = patterns.Filename(
    "/zone/home/project/collection/objectname.txt"
    )
fname.path
fname.params
fname.destination_path
fname.log_result()
```

We can change the destination path whenever we want;
in fact, when the file passes validation its pattern will override it.

```{python}
fname.destination_path = "/zone/home/project/bad_files/{{filename}}"
fname.log_result()
```

These attributes can also be set on initiation.
```{python}
fname2 = patterns.Filename(
    path="/zone/home/project/collection/dataset.csv",
    params={"project": "/zone/home/project/"},
    invalid_destination_pattern="{{project}}/bad_files/{{filename}}",
)
fname2.log_result()
```

## The `Pattern` class

The `Pattern` class is initiated with a regular expression `pattern`,
a list of functions for `additional_validation`, a `jinja2` template
for a `destination_pattern` and a `jinja_environment`. All these arguments are optional and have default values,
so it is entirely possible to try out the class as below:

```{python}
p = patterns.Pattern()
p.pattern  # group 'filename' matching words
p.additional_validation  # empty list
p.destination_pattern  # just the filename
```

A `Filename` can be validated against a `Pattern` with
just the `validate_against_pattern()` method. For a case with
a simple regular expression and no validation functions,
this may be overkill.
The result of this function is the output of `log_result()`
after validation.

```{python}
fname.validate_against_pattern(p)
```

Let's try creating a `Pattern` with a custom regular expression,
a validation function and a destination pattern.
The function `check_txt()` below
takes the dictionary of filename properties as input and
_returns a string if something is wrong, nothing otherwise_.
The `validate_against_pattern()` method first matches the
path of the `Filename` against the regex pattern, and if it
succeeds, it updates the `params` dictionary with the values
of the named groups. Only then does it go over the list of
validation functions, and if any of them fail, breaks and
considers the filename invalid.

```{python}

def check_txt(params):
    if params.get("ext", "") != "txt":
        return "We only accept txt files."

p2 = patterns.Pattern(
    pattern = r"/zone/home/(?P<project>[^/]+)/.+\.(?P<ext>.+)$",
    additional_validation = [check_txt],
    destination_pattern = "/zone/home/{{project}}/good_file/{{filename}}"
    )
p2.pattern
p2.additional_validation
p.destination_pattern
```

We can now validate the `Filename` against this pattern.

```{python}
fname.validate_against_pattern(p2)
```

Because this validation requires the extension to be "txt",
a file with a different extension will not pass.
Of course, just forcing the extension to be "txt" can be done
with the regex as well, but
(i) this is just a simple example for illustration, and
(ii) validation functions also offer custom messages.

```{python}
fname2.validate_against_pattern(p2)
```

## The `PatternSet` class

There is no message update in the `Filename` log just because it has
failed to match a `Pattern` unless it has passed the regex match.
The idea is that a `Filename` might be evaluated against an ordered
collection of `Pattern`s, each with potentially different regexes and
validation functions. This collection can be gathered in a `PatternSet`.

This class can be initiated with a list of `validation_functions`
and a dictionary of `jinja2` `filters`, but both are optional
and can be added later.
A single `Pattern` can be added with the `add_pattern()` method,
which allows to choose whether the `Pattern` should inherit the `jinja2`
environment of the `PatternSet` (e.g. in case you have conflicting filters).
Multiple `Pattern`s can be added with the `patterns` setter,
which forces inheritance of the filters. In both cases,
`validation_functions` of the `PatternSet` are appended to each of the
patterns (as long as the pattern is added after the function).

```{python}
#| include: false
fname2 = patterns.Filename(
    path="/zone/home/project/collection/dataset.csv",
    params={"project": "/zone/home/project/"},
    invalid_destination_pattern="{{project}}/bad_files/{{filename}}",
)
```
```{python}
patternset = patterns.PatternSet()
patternset.patterns  # empty
patternset.patterns = [p2, p]
patternset.patterns
fname2.validate(patternset)
fname.validate(patternset)
```
